title: JSP-000868: record Lean proof
body:
## Submission type

- [ ] Mathematical solver information
- [x] Lean proof or formalization author information

The complete mathematical solution is by Erdős–Herzog–Piranian (1958) and Pommerenke (1959) (see Problem and Formal statement below); this submission claims only the Lean formalization and records it in the catalog.

## Problem

- Problem: JSP-000868 — "If a polynomial's unit-modulus sublevel set is connected, must it lie in a disk of radius two?"
- Problem ID(s): JSP-000868
- Original problem source and exact location (page, section or problem number): Erdős–Herzog–Piranian, "Metric properties of polynomials", J. Analyse Math. (1958), DOI 10.1007/bf02790232; and Pommerenke, "On some problems by Erdős, Herzog and Piranian", Michigan Math. J. (1959), 221–225 (Jensen-argument proof).
- Current entry and proposed change: Catalog change in this PR: only the JSP-000868 "Lean proof" field in problems/catalog-0801-0900.md, from "No" to "Yes" with a link to the Lean source and formalization contributor @universe2explorer.
- Related issue, if any: None
- Related PRs and how this contribution differs, including any issue found in an existing submission and supporting evidence (optional): None known. This PR records the Lean proof for JSP-000868.
- For solver/publication updates: public proof or publication, relevant theorem/pages, version or date: Erdős–Herzog–Piranian (1958), DOI 10.1007/bf02790232; Pommerenke, Michigan Math. J. (1959), 221–225. Answer: yes — for monic nonconstant complex polynomials, a connected unit lemniscate lies in a closed disk of radius two.

## Formal statement

For Lean contributions only. Repeat the theorem details for each problem.

- Complete mathematical solution (provided earlier or in this PR): public proof or publication, relevant theorem/pages, version or date: Erdős–Herzog–Piranian, "Metric properties of polynomials", J. Analyse Math. (1958), DOI 10.1007/bf02790232; and Pommerenke, "On some problems by Erdős, Herzog and Piranian", Michigan Math. J. (1959), 221–225 (Jensen-argument proof). Answer: yes — for monic nonconstant complex polynomials, a connected unit lemniscate lies in a closed disk of radius two.
- Mathematical review reference or current review status: The JSP-000868 catalog entry records the problem as Solved, with the Erdős–Herzog–Piranian (1958) and Pommerenke (1959) publications above.
- Formal statement location, pinned to a full commit SHA: https://github.com/universe2explorer/jsp-000868-lean/blob/065fcd8d1c4b90f981fe837dc8d31257e4397e09/JSP000868/Main.lean
- Fully qualified target theorem name: `JSP000868.jsp000868`
- Statement origin (maintainer-approved reference and version, or proposed statement requiring review): The JSP-000868 catalog entry, as formalized below.
- Correspondence to the original problem: definitions, assumptions, quantifiers, conclusion and all required cases; explain any differences from an approved statement: Formal statement (as formalized): theorem `JSP000868.jsp000868` — for `f : ℂ[X]` with `f.Monic`, if `{z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1}` is connected, then there exists `c : ℂ` with `{z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1} ⊆ Metric.ball c 2` (in the proof, c is the root centroid). Scope note: the formalization uses the monic normalization and the strict sublevel set, as stated here.

## Proof submission

For Lean contributions only. Use the original repository containing your contribution, owned by your submitting account or an organization. For an organization repository, supply verifiable contribution evidence under Attribution.
**Link the proof; do not commit Lean source here.**

- Lean formalization: external repository https://github.com/universe2explorer/jsp-000868-lean, branch main, pinned commit 065fcd8d1c4b90f981fe837dc8d31257e4397e09. Main theorem `JSP000868.jsp000868` in JSP000868/Main.lean; supporting results `JSP000868.JensenWeight.weighted_jensen` and `JSP000868.oneDim_bound`. Toolchain: Lean v4.33.0, Mathlib v4.33.0.

```json
[
  {
    "repository": "https://github.com/universe2explorer/jsp-000868-lean",
    "branch": "main",
    "commit": "065fcd8d1c4b90f981fe837dc8d31257e4397e09"
  }
]
```

- Proof file at the selected commit and fully qualified theorem name: JSP000868/Main.lean — `JSP000868.jsp000868`; supporting results `JSP000868.JensenWeight.weighted_jensen` and `JSP000868.oneDim_bound`
- How the proof establishes the formal statement above, including any separate verification entry: The proof formalizes the Jensen-argument approach: for a monic nonconstant polynomial whose strict unit sublevel set is connected, every point of that set lies within distance two of the root centroid, giving the stated inclusion in `Metric.ball c 2`.

## Reproduction

For Lean contributions only.

- Exact Lean version and `lean-toolchain` path: Lean v4.33.0, Mathlib v4.33.0. Toolchain file: lean-toolchain at the root of the Lean repository.
- Pinned dependencies (including mathlib, if used) and manifest path: Mathlib v4.33.0; manifest path: lake-manifest.json at the root of the Lean repository.
- Build instructions pinned to the selected commit: https://github.com/universe2explorer/jsp-000868-lean/tree/065fcd8d1c4b90f981fe837dc8d31257e4397e09
- Commands for setup, clean build and checking each target theorem; include a separate statement-to-proof check if needed: `lake exe cache get && lake build` completes successfully (3484 jobs; independently reproduced 2026-10-12).
- Axiom audit command and output for each target (for example, `#print axioms Fully.Qualified.theoremName`): Axiom audit (`#print axioms`) for `JSP000868.jsp000868` and `JSP000868.oneDim_bound` shows only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] — no sorry, no admit, no native_decide.

## Pre-submission Lean verification (optional)

- Method/tool and version, if available: `lake exe cache get && lake build` and `#print axioms`, with Lean v4.33.0 / Mathlib v4.33.0.
- Checked repository and full commit SHA; identify any difference from the submitted version: https://github.com/universe2explorer/jsp-000868-lean at 065fcd8d1c4b90f981fe837dc8d31257e4397e09; no difference from the submitted version. Independently reproduced 2026-10-12.
- Verification date, actual conclusion and limitations: 2026-10-12; `lake exe cache get && lake build` completes successfully (3484 jobs). Scope is as stated in the formal statement above (monic normalization, strict sublevel set).
- Summary of statement correspondence, coverage, Lean checks and trust dependencies: The main theorem corresponds to the JSP-000868 statement as formalized above; axiom audit for `JSP000868.jsp000868` and `JSP000868.oneDim_bound` shows only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] — no sorry, no admit, no native_decide.
- Report in this PR or external report/log/evidence links, if available: This PR.

## Attribution

- Mathematical solver(s) and contribution, if applicable: Erdős–Herzog–Piranian (1958) and Pommerenke (1959), as cited above.
- Lean formalization author(s) and contribution, if applicable: @universe2explorer — Lean formalization in https://github.com/universe2explorer/jsp-000868-lean. Formalization contributors: @universe2explorer.
- Independent verifier(s), if any: None named; the build was independently reproduced 2026-10-12 as stated above.
- Public authorship evidence; for an organization repository, link verifiable evidence connecting your account to the claimed proof files/theorems (such as merged PRs, attributable changes or project authorship records). Explain mismatches between authors, accounts and proposed credits: The Lean repository is owned by the submitting account universe2explorer, at pinned commit 065fcd8d1c4b90f981fe837dc8d31257e4397e09 on branch main.

- [x] The submitted result fully solves the original problem. Any submitted Lean proof is complete at the specified comm
